title: Compact durable-job result format
hypothesis: Removing the full command from repeated job results reduces model input without losing verification evidence or worsening task completion.
falsified_if: Activation fails, either arm fails artifact or completion verification, or compact results regress latency or estimated cost beyond the registered tolerance.
local_evidence: /tmp/lca/logs/lca-20260916-191522-707162.log and matching JSONL, calls 26:5, 26:7, 26:8, 26:10. Four waits returned 9729–10410 characters dominated by a 9694-character command. Offline replay preserved status/output while reducing responses to 217–898 bytes.
deterministic_outcomes: successful durable verification of final artifact
decision_rule: Seed 917; four runs, one per arm and scenario; simple control first and adjacent coding pair randomized. Freeze all source including C, fixture/grader and prompt/config hashes in campaign manifest before live calls. Change only command formatting via eval-only jobs.describe wrapper; execution, wait deadlines, tool schemas, models and prompts are identical. Maximum four launches, $2 standard-equivalent between-run cost threshold (one-run overshoot possible), 300 active seconds. Stop on any artifact, protocol or activation failure; retain failed resources. Advance only if every run passes, coding job-result bytes decrease at least 80%, coding elapsed time and estimated cost each are no more than 10% worse, and coding model calls do not increase. Otherwise record mixed/negative evidence and no efficiency adoption claim. Screen can only justify fresh broader validation; it cannot establish long-task improvements or justify notifications. Existing user-authorized correctness fixes remain separate from this formatter-only comparison.
